subject: physics_2
question_text: What is Doppler shift? Obtain an expression for the apparent frequency of sound heard when the observer is in motion with respect to a source at rest?

verification.note: The 1+1+2+2+2 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it — the figure carries 0 marks because the question does not ask for a diagram. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: with the observer approaching a stationary source the sound reaches the observer at the relative speed V + V₀, so t₁ = L/(V + V₀); t₂ = T + (L − V₀T)/(V + V₀); T′ = t₂ − t₁ = T·V/(V + V₀); n′ = 1/T′ = n(V + V₀)/V > n, and n′ = n(V − V₀)/V < n when the observer recedes. This is the moving-OBSERVER case — the wavelength in the air is unchanged and only the rate of crest arrival changes, which is why V₀ appears in the NUMERATOR here and Vₛ in the denominator on the moving-source card. The book prints the question as "with respect a source at rest", dropping the word "to"; the wording is preserved as printed.

recall_prompt: Say the derivation in order — what Doppler shift means, the arrival times of the two crests, the apparent period, and the apparent frequency.

steps.label: Doppler shift defined
steps.mark_note: Difference between apparent and actual frequency
lines: Doppler shift is the difference between
the apparent frequency heard by the
observer and the actual frequency
produced by the source.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Define the shift as a difference of two frequencies, then begin the derivation.
steps.why: The rest of the answer builds the apparent frequency n′; the definition fixes what the question is finally asking for, which is the gap between n′ and n.
common_mistakes: Calling the shift the apparent frequency itself. The shift is the difference n′ − n.
Leaving out the definition. The question asks for it before the derivation.

recall.must_convey: That Doppler shift is the difference between the apparent frequency heard and the actual frequency produced.
accept: difference between apparent and actual frequency
the change in frequency due to relative motion
reject: the first crest takes L by V plus V nought

steps.memory_tip: Shift means a difference — apparent frequency minus actual frequency.

steps.label: The geometry
steps.margin_note: S stays fixed; the observer starts at O and reaches O′ one time period later, a distance V₀T nearer to S.
steps.why: The picture holds the one difference from the moving-source case: the separation shrinks because the OBSERVER moved, while the crests already in the air keep their original spacing.
common_mistakes: Moving the source in this figure. Here S is at rest and only O moves.

recall.must_convey: That S stays fixed while the observer moves from O to O′, a distance V₀T, so the second crest covers L − V₀T.
accept: mark S, O and O dash
the observer moves V nought T toward the source
the second crest has less distance left
reject: T dash is T into V over V plus V nought

steps.memory_tip: Three ticks on a line — S, O′, O — with L, L − V₀T and V₀T between them.

steps.label: Set-up and the first crest
lines: A source S at rest and an observer O are
a distance L apart. The source emits
sound of frequency n and time period T;
V is the speed of sound in air.
The observer moves toward S with
velocity V₀, so the sound reaches the
observer at the relative speed V + V₀.
The first crest covers the distance L:
steps.margin_note: One mark. Name every symbol, then write the relative speed V + V₀ before the first arrival time.
steps.why: The relative speed is the whole difference from the moving-source case: the sound still travels at V through the air, but the observer runs into the crests, so they arrive at the rate set by V + V₀.
common_mistakes: Writing t₁ = L/V. The observer is approaching, so the closing speed is V + V₀.
Leaving symbols undefined. n, T, V, V₀ and L must each be introduced.

recall.must_convey: That the separation is L, the observer approaches at V₀, and the first crest arrives after t₁ = L/(V + V₀).
accept: relative speed V plus V nought
t one is L by V plus V nought
reject: the second crest travels L minus V nought T

steps.memory_tip: The observer runs into the sound, so the speeds add: V + V₀ under the L.

steps.label: The second crest
lines: The source releases the second crest one
time period T later. In that time the
observer has moved a distance V₀T
toward S and stands at O′, so the
second crest covers only L − V₀T:
steps.margin_note: Two marks: the shortened distance L − V₀T, and the T added for the later start.
steps.why: Both pieces of t₂ carry a mark: the crest is emitted T later, but it meets an observer who has already closed part of the gap.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the leading T. The second crest is emitted at time T, and only then travels.
Writing L + V₀T. The observer approaches, so the remaining distance shrinks.

recall.must_convey: That the second crest leaves T later and covers L − V₀T at V + V₀, so t₂ = T + (L − V₀T)/(V + V₀).
accept: covers only L minus V nought T
t two is T plus L minus V nought T over V plus V nought
reject: t one is L by V plus V nought

steps.memory_tip: Later start (+T), shorter road (L − V₀T) — write both, in that order.

steps.label: Apparent time period
lines: The observer receives the two crests a
time T′ apart — the apparent time
period:

lines.text: T′ = T + (L − V₀T)/(V + V₀) − L/(V + V₀)

steps.margin_note: Two marks: subtract the arrival times, watch L cancel, and take T outside the bracket.
steps.why: L cancels because the result cannot depend on how far apart the two started, only on how fast the gap closes — any surviving L is the signal that a term was dropped.
common_mistakes: Keeping L in the final expression. The two L/(V + V₀) terms cancel exactly.
Sign slip in the bracket. Approach must shorten the period, so T′ < T.

recall.must_convey: That subtracting the arrival times cancels L and gives T′ = T·V/(V + V₀).
accept: subtract t one from t two
T dash is T into V over V plus V nought

steps.memory_tip: If L survives the subtraction, redo it — a rate result cannot hold a distance.

steps.label: Apparent frequency
lines: The apparent frequency is the reciprocal
of the apparent time period:
n′ > n: the heard frequency is higher
when the observer moves toward the
source. If the observer moves away from
the source, V₀ reverses sign:
The Doppler shift is n′ − n = ± nV₀/V.
steps.margin_note: Two marks: invert T′ to get n′, then state both cases and close with the shift the question named.
steps.why: Here V₀ sits in the numerator, while the moving-source formula carries Vₛ in the denominator — the two cases are not the same algebra, and quoting the shift n′ − n answers the word the question opened with.
common_mistakes: Writing n′ = n·V/(V + V₀). That is the period, not the frequency; invert it.
Using the moving-source form nV/(V − Vₛ) here. The observer case puts the sum on top.

recall.must_convey: That n′ = 1/T′ = n(V + V₀)/V, higher than n for approach, with (V − V₀) for recession.
accept: n into V plus V nought by V
minus V nought when moving away

steps.memory_tip: Observer moving: the V₀ goes on TOP. Source moving: the Vₛ goes on the BOTTOM.

insider_note: The two Doppler long answers differ in one place only — a moving observer puts V₀ in the numerator, a moving source puts Vₛ in the denominator. Writing the source formula for this question loses the last four marks.
